mainMenuInventory.nativeContract: Inactive in source; not exposed as actionable toolbar button

sourceBoundaries: Model supports named simultaneous bars, ordered compositions, per-bar visibility and icon/text mode, standard/custom placement on top/bottom/left/right or floating, bounded dock order, remembered return dock edge/order and finite bounded saved floating rectangles, persistent identity, reset and bounded known command IDs.

Standard toolbar all-side docking/floating is directly established by source flags plus documented CMFCToolBar implementation. User-toolbar creation and Customize are explicit; individual new-bar initial placement is inherited framework behavior.
Native docking uses AppKit strips and owned NSPanel windows; this is an adaptation, not a binary MFC docking implementation. Pane auto-hide flags do not certify toolbar auto-hide semantics.

Quick move receipts capture epoch, toolbar ID, occurrence index, expected command and source composition; accepted transfer applies atomically without executing commands. Duplicate executable commands, stale payloads, invalid offsets and missing bars are refused; repeated spacers remain distinct occurrences.

Primary references explicitly prove Alt-drag relocation. Exact source copy-key modifier and outside-drop deletion were not established; no automatic outside-drop removal or speculative copy gesture should be claimed. Model copy helper is distinct from verified native gesture support.
Output-pane context popup Clear/Hide is not the scanned main menu; no nonexistent clear-output operation invented.
Disabled Help Finder remains excluded; recent-file contents remain dynamic menu state, not persisted executable commands.
validation: Implementation and primary-source mapping only. Placement/drag batch tests and builds are deferred to the root grouped checkpoint; no physical drag, VoiceOver, signed sandbox or complete MFC layout parity certified.

primaryFrameworkReferences.contract: CMFCToolBar::EnableDocking sets AFX_CBRS_FLOAT; directly establishes floating capability for source standard toolbar.
EnableQuickCustomization allows Alt-drag moving toolbar buttons to another location; generic class supports drag-and-drop between toolbars and menus.

Framework constructs new user toolbar; source override delegates creation and then adds Customize. Exact initial user-toolbar docking is framework-inherited rather than explicitly configured in this source override.
Docking to enabled sides and detaching into a floating mini-frame are MFC toolbar operations.

CPane::DockPane DM_DBL_CLICK restores most recent docking position, and double-click undocking restores most recent floating position. Native fields retain last dock edge/order and floating rectangle.
